items.title: Iran and Israel say they will pause strikes but warn of retaliation if ceasefire breached again
items.description: Israel's PM says his country is holding fire "at the moment", after Iran's armed forces said they had stopped military action.

items.title: Iran's strike on Israel suggests the regime's sense of resilience is growing
items.description: Iran's decision to risk jeopardising peace talks may reflect how its leaders view their current position, writes BBC Persian editor Amir Azimi.

items.title: At least 35 dead after major earthquake strikes southern Philippines
items.description: The magnitude-7.8 quake triggered small tsunami waves in the Philippines, Indonesia and Japan.

items.title: Armenia's pro-West government wins election despite Russian pressure
items.description: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's Civil Contract Party secures nearly 50% of the vote, comfortably beating the other contenders.

items.title: Malawians repatriated from South Africa amid xenophobia concerns
items.description: Malawi is among several African nations transporting their citizens out of the country following reports of violence against migrants.

items.title: Jailed crypto founder Sam Bankman-Fried seeks Trump pardon
items.description: The former leader of crypto platform FTX, currently serving a 25-year sentence, on Monday officially applied to be pardoned.

items.title: Watch: Southern Lights timelapse filmed from space
items.description: This occurrence of aurora australis, or Southern Lights, was captured by NASA astronaut Jessica Meir.

items.title: 'City's gonna be crazy:' Knicks run electrifies NYC, as Trump's attendance locks down arena
items.description: The Knicks' stunning winning streak has energised New York as the team prepares for the third game of the NBA Finals at home.

items.title: Stock market jitters remain amid tech fears and renewed Middle East attacks
items.description: Markets in Asia are hit by a tech sell-off, and oil is volatile as Iran and Israel launch attacks on each other.

items.title: Eriksen at home and 'doing well' after collapse
items.description: Christian Eriksen says he is "doing well" and is at home with his family following his collapse in Sunday's game against Ukraine.

items.title: Somali referee Artan barred from entering USA
items.description: Omar Artan, who was set to be the first Somali to referee at the World Cup finals, is dropped from the list of officials after he was denied entry to the United States.

items.title: Kenya's ex-chief justice arrested at protest against building on national park
items.description: Activists allege there is a plan to build a car park on protected land belonging to a wildlife sanctuary.
